newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault-Peugeot merger a bad idea - Borotra.
newsitem.headline: Renault-Peugeot merger a bad idea - Borotra.

text.p: French Industry Minister Franck Borotra said on Wednesday that it would make no sense to merge French carmakers Renault SA and PSA Peugeot Citroen because they would not complement each other well.
"It's a bad idea because they tend to have the same strengths and the same weaknesses," Borotra told Reuters in an interview. He said they also had different corporate cultures.

The chairmen of the two car companies have said they would oppose a merger as a way of solving difficulties, which are due mainly to their over dependence on the slow-growing and fiercely competitive European car market.

Borotra reiterated he thought there was room in the auto industry for both the PSA group and Renault, currently ranked fifth and sixth of Europe's six mass volume manufacturers, but they needed to multiply partnerships to reduce costs and increase exports outside Europe.

He reiterated that Renault's restructuring, including the proposed closure of the Vilvoorde assembly plant in Belgium, were essential to its survival. Renault is 46 percent owned by the French state. It reported a 5.25 billion franc loss for 1996, including 3.9 billion in charges and the PSA group saw its profit shrink by more than half last year.
